slides.0.title: Sweet and fortified wines
slides.0.subtitle: Vin de Constance, Muscadel, Jerepigo, Cape Port
slides.1.title: Classifying sweet wines
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Natural Sweet
slides.1.highlights.0.content: More than 20 g/L residual sugar, with sweetness from variety and ripeness rather than noble rot; example: Klein Constantia's Vin de Constance
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Noble Late Harvest
slides.1.highlights.1.content: More than 50 g/L (often 100–150 g/L, sometimes 200 g/L) with botrytis; example: Nederburg Edelkeur
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Straw wine
slides.1.highlights.2.content: More than 30 g/L, with grapes dried on straw mats after picking; examples: Mullineux and De Trafford from Chenin Blanc
slides.1.content: These thresholds come from trade-media summaries; check the regulations under the Liquor Products Act for the formal text.
slides.2.title: Vin de Constance
slides.2.highlights.0.title: History
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Constantia's sweet wines were famous in the 19th century; phylloxera and mildew ended the historic era; Duggie Jooste began the revival at Klein Constantia in 1980
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The modern wine
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Klein Constantia's modern version was first made in 1986 and released in 1990; made from Muscat de Frontignan as a botrytis-free, raisined dessert wine; in some years pickers go through the vineyard up to seven times
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Other descendants
slides.2.content: Vin de Constance is a Natural Sweet, not a botrytised wine; a common point of confusion.
slides.3.title: Fortified wines
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Muscadel
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Fortified and made from Muscat: white Muscadel uses Muscat d'Alexandrie (Hanepoot) or Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains, red uses Muscat de Frontignan; fermentation is halted by adding grape spirit, giving 15–22% abv
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Jerepigo
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Never fermented: grape juice with added spirit, generally brandy
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Cape Port styles
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Centred on Calitzdorp with Portuguese varieties such as Touriga Nacional; since 2012 names such as Cape Vintage and Cape Tawny are required
slides.3.content: Both Muscadel and Jerepigo are fortified, but Muscadel is stopped partway through fermentation while Jerepigo is never fermented.
Which class of sweet wine is Vin de Constance?
B. Grape juice plus spirit, never fermented
What was the first vintage of Klein Constantia's modern Vin de Constance?
Since 2012 how must Calitzdorp's Port-style wines be named?
B. Cape Vintage / Cape Tawny etc.
